english.title: Attempt to indecently assault a boy under the age of 16 years
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) attempted to indecently assault **(..SPECIFY THE NAME OF THE BOY..), a boy under 16 years of age
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
attempted to indecently assault
a boy under 16 years of age

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
THIS OFFENCE IS NOW OBSOLETE

(i) A victim under 16 years of age CANNOT consent to any form of indecent assault, and, since the case of R v K 2000 Times 7.11.00 it has been confirmed that this is an issue of strict liability. Click on the link for section 15(1) (in legislation above) and read the notes for more.
(ii) This offence is included in Schedule 1 to the Sex Offenders Act 1997, therefore a person convicted or cautioned for this offence must comply with the requirements of section 2 of that Act.
(iii) This offence is included in Schedule 2 to the Sex Offenders Act 1997, therefore a person committing this offence outside the United Kingdom may in certain circumstances be prosecuted for that offence in England, Wales or Northern Ireland.
(iv) Repealed by s.140 of and Schedule 7 to the Sexual Offences Act 2003

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Ten years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
